title: The Detroja Cyclic Research Model: Quantum Hardware Execution, Technical Benchmarks, and Comparative Analysis Report
abstract: This report details the empirical research, technical benchmarks, and comparative performance analysis of The Detroja Cyclic Research Model executed on real 156-qubit quantum hardware (IBM Quantum Heron) and evaluated against global Non-Equilibrium Quantum Field Dynamics (NEQFD) theory benchmarks. It covers hardware benchmarks, quantum noise and error analysis, cross-platform architecture readiness using Python Cirq for Google Quantum processors, and optimized execution modules.

title: Georacoon - testing and example dataset
abstract: This dataset provides geographic raster datasets (GeoTIFF) used as example and test data forthe GeoRacoon Python package. None of this data is shipped with the installed package, it exists for contributors and example scripts working from a git clone, fetched on demand. All source datasets are third-party data, redistributed here under their own upstreamlicenses (not GeoRacoon's own MIT code license). Per-dataset provenance and licensedetail below. Alterations: reprojected from the EPSG:3035 version (see test/ below) to Sinusoidal CRS. test.zip switzerland_lc-8-reclass_2012_CLC_epsg3035.tifCORINE Land Cover (CLC) 2012. Provider: European Environment Agency (EEA) / Copernicus Land Monitoring Service. License: Copernicus / EEA free re-use (attribution required). Alterations: cropped to Switzerland extent; reclassified from the full CLC nomenclature down to 8 aggregate classes. switzerland_lc-area-fraction_2015_CGLS-LC100_epsg2056.tifCopernicus Global Land Cover 100 m (CGLS-LC100), 2015 epoch. Provider: Copernicus Land Monitoring Service / VITO. License: Copernicus free & open data policy (reproduction, distribution, adaptation permitted; source must be acknowledged). Alterations: reprojected from the Sinusoidal version in examples/ to EPSG:2056 (Swiss LV95). switzerland_ndvi-binned-mean_2015_LANDSAT-8_epsg3035.tifLandsat-8 composite, 2015. Provider: NASA LP DAAC / USGS. License: Public domain (federally created data; no copyright restriction; USGS credit requested). Alterations: cloud-masked; NDVI calculated and DOY-binned, median per bin, mean across bins; reprojected to EPSG:3035. title: 自适应量子态的动态能量控制
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum state control centered around dynamic energy modulation. We propose a self-adaptive algorithm that intelligently adjusts key quantum parameter values, specifically frequency and phase, to optimize the performance of quantum computation. The core mechanism involves a hierarchical feedback loop that continuously refines these parameters based on observed outcomes, resulting in enhanced qubit coherence and reduced error rates. This approach offers a significant advancement over traditional static control methods, potentially unlocking new capabilities within quantum computing. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the efficacy of this method in enhancing quantum coherence and exploring its impact on quantum algorithm complexity.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Networks
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, holding the potential for revolutionary technologies in secure communication, quantum computing, and metrology. However, maintaining and manipulating entangled states is a significant challenge due to their fragility and susceptibility to decoherence. This paper explores the development of a novel quantum entanglement network utilizing a self-adaptive self-assembly mechanism. We propose a system where quantum entanglement networks are dynamically constructed and expanded through the application of "quantum pulses" – precisely modulated interactions designed to subtly alter the network's structure. This approach offers the potential for automatic network expansion and enhanced quantum information transfer, circumventing the limitations of traditional, manually designed architectures. The core mechanism revolves around the controlled manipulation of quantum entanglement through a carefully orchestrated sequence of pulses. This work demonstrates the feasibility of building a self-expanding entanglement network, highlighting the potential for significant advancements in quantum information processing.

title: Relational Reasoning with Graph Transformers and Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Graph transformers have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in processing graph-structured data, particularly in tasks like node classification and link prediction. However, a significant limitation remains their struggle with complex relational reasoning – the ability to understand intricate connections and dependencies between entities within a graph. This paper proposes a novel architecture that addresses this limitation by integrating graph transformers with knowledge graphs. Our approach leverages explicit relational embeddings derived from a structured knowledge graph to provide the transformer with a richer understanding of the relationships between nodes. We hypothesize that incorporating this knowledge will significantly improve the transformer's ability to perform sophisticated relational reasoning tasks. The core idea is to augment the standard graph transformer architecture with a mechanism that explicitly encodes relational information, thereby enhancing the model's capacity to infer and understand complex relationships within graph data. We evaluate our method on several benchmark graph reasoning datasets and demonstrate its superior performance compared to existing graph transformer models. The results validate the effectiveness of combining the strengths of graph transformers and knowledge graphs for enhanced relational understanding.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Causal Inference
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed causal inference leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional methods of causal inference face challenges in distributed systems, including latency, information silos, and difficulty in establishing robust causal relationships across geographically dispersed data sources. Our framework utilizes multiple quantum sensors to collect data from a distributed system. Quantum entanglement is then employed to correlate the measurement results from these sensors in real-time. This correlation is achieved through quantum entanglement-based quantum teleportation, facilitating the rapid propagation and synchronization of causal information. A causal inference model is constructed based on the characteristics of the entangled states, enabling real-time reasoning. The core claim is that this approach allows for real-time, high-precision inference of causal relationships in distributed systems, effectively addressing the limitations of conventional methods. We demonstrate the potential of exploiting quantum mechanics to achieve efficient causal inference in distributed environments.

title: Distributed Fusion Filtering with Prediction Compensation for Multi-Sensor Systems Subject to DoS-Attack-Induced Packet Dropouts
abstract: This paper investigates the distributed fusion estimation problem for multi-sensor cyber-physical systems (CPSs), where the communication channels from local estimators to the fusion center are subject to random packet dropouts. Packet dropouts induced by either network congestion or intermittent denial-of-service (DoS) attacks are modeled as Bernoulli random variables. When a local estimate is lost, a prediction compensation strategy is adopted at the fusion center, where the missing data are replaced by their one-step predictors. By constructing an augmented state consisting of the original state, local prediction errors, and virtual measurements, the multi-sensor system is transformed into a stochastic system with random parameter matrices and one-step autocorrelated noises. Based on the transformed system, a distributed state fusion (DSF) filter is proposed via the innovation analysis method, whose filter gain depends on the successful-reception probabilities. The stability of the proposed DSF filter is analyzed, and a sufficient condition for the existence of a steady-state filter is obtained. The steady-state gain can be pre-computed offline, thereby reducing the online computational burden. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

title: Research data for Generation of fully phase controlled two-photon entangled states
abstract: The file contains all the data necessary to replicate the figures in the publication 'Generation of fully phase controlled two-photon entangled states'. The individual spreadsheets are for each figure with the data therein corresponding to the sub-figures, if applicable.AbstractControl over the internal states of trapped ions makes them the ideal system to generate single and two-photon states. Coupling a single ion to an optical cavity enables efficient emission of single photons into a single spatial mode and grants control over their temporal shape, phase, and frequency. Using the long coherence time of the ion’s internal states and employing a scheme to protect the coherence of the ion-cavity interaction, we demonstrate the generation of a two-photon entangled state with full control over the phase. Initially, ion-photon entanglement is generated. A second photon is subsequently generated, mapping the ion’s state onto the second photon. By adjusting the drive field the phase of the entangled state can be fully controlled. We implement this scheme in the most resource efficient way by utilizing a single 40Ca+ ion coupled to an optical cavity and demonstrate the generation of a two-photon entangled stated with full phase control with a fidelity of up to 82%.

title: A knowledge-aware graph-based framework for document-level event extraction
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of document-level event extraction as a critical step toward automated knowledge acquisition for intelligent systems. Extracting structured event knowledge from unstructured text is essential for downstream knowledge-based applications such as knowledge graph construction, decision support, and intelligent question answering. However, existing approaches struggle to effectively capture long-range dependencies and complex inter-event relationships within documents while maintaining computational efficiency. To address these challenges, we propose a novel knowledge-aware framework, the Graph Convolutional Network with Pseudo-trigger Combination Recognition(GCN-PCR). The proposed model explicitly represents entities, mentions, and sentences as interconnected nodes in a relational graph, enabling structured modeling of semantic dependencies and co-reference information across document contexts. Furthermore, the pseudo-trigger combination strategy enhances the identification of event structures by improving the robustness of event boundary detection and argument association. Extensive experiments on two public datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. More importantly, our framework provides a scalable and effective solution for transforming unstructured textual data into structured event knowledge, facilitating its integration into knowledge-based systems.

title: Quantum-enhanced hybrid-model compression using knowledge distillation
abstract: Abstract Quantum computing has emerged as a promising paradigm for addressing computational tasks intractable for classical systems, leveraging quantum mechanical principles such as superposition and entanglement to efficiently explore high-dimensional solution spaces. In recent years, hybrid quantum-classical approaches have gained increasing attention as a means to exploit the representational power of quantum systems while preserving the practicality of classical machine learning frameworks. This paper presents a study on quantum-enhanced model compression via feature-based knowledge distillation, in which a large classical neural network (the teacher) transfers knowledge to a substantially smaller hybrid student model. The proposed hybrid quantum-classical student architecture incorporates a parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) implemented in Qiskit, employing a linear $$\varvec{R_y}$$ angle-encoding feature map followed by an EfficientSU2 variational ansatz, with features bounded through a $$\varvec{\tanh (\cdot )\times \frac{\pi }{2}}$$ scaling to ensure stable gradient propagation. Gradient computation is performed via Reverse-Mode (adjoint) differentiation through the StatevectorEstimator primitive, which provides exact, shot-noise-free gradients at the cost of a single forward–backward pass per optimization step. The hybrid student is compared against a parameter-matched purely classical student under strict 1:1 parameter parity across a six-task binary benchmark spanning MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, as well as a four-class multi-class benchmark, totaling eleven classification experiments. A hardware validation experiment is additionally conducted on the IQM Garnet 20-qubit quantum processor using the Parameter-Shift Rule. The results indicate that the hybrid student outperforms its classical counterpart in five of six binary tasks (83%) and in the two hardest multi-class configurations, with advantages most pronounced in high-confusion regimes where compact classical classifiers approach the limits of their expressive capacity. On real quantum hardware, accuracy decreases from 99.04% in noiseless simulation to 80.50%, reflecting the impact of gate noise, readout errors, and transpilation overhead. While the hybrid model demonstrates improved parameter efficiency and expressive capacity, it incurs higher computational overhead and exhibits greater epoch-to-epoch training variability relative to classical baselines. We discuss practical limitations related to noise, scalability, and current hardware constraints, and identify directions for future work including hardware-efficient gradient estimation and advanced error mitigation protocols. Overall, our findings suggest that variational quantum circuits can serve as compact yet expressive components within neural compression schemes, with their representational advantage most effectively realized in binary and high-ambiguity classification scenarios.

Overall, our findings suggest that variational quantum circuits can serve as compact yet expressive components within neural compression schemes, with their representational advantage most effectively realized in binary and high-ambiguity classification scenarios.

title: Evaluation of MLLM-Agnostic Plug-and-Play Keyframe Selection Methods for Long Video Understanding
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) cannot process every frame of a long video because of limitations in visual-token and computational budgets. Three primary approaches have been proposed to enhance their long-video understanding capabilities: (i) Retraining an MLLM on a large video corpus and/or extending its input length; (ii) Training an adapter for a specific MLLM that takes the entire video and the query as input and selects the most relevant video frames; and (iii) Developing a training-free, plug-and-play (PaP) adapter that is MLLM-agnostic. We refer to the third approach as PaP keyframe selection. A PaP method may use only candidate video frames without considering the query, or it may use both candidate video frames and the query. The first approach is prohibitively expensive. The second approach requires substantial training time and computational resources, but it is accessible to many because an adapter contains significantly fewer trainable parameters than an entire MLLM. The third approach has the lowest computational cost and is therefore broadly accessible. To the best of our knowledge, only five PaP methods have been reported within the past year. All of these methods have been evaluated on one or more video question-answering benchmarks and have demonstrated improvements in long-video understanding. However, the methods were evaluated on different benchmarks using different MLLMs. We present a comprehensive evaluation of these five methods using three MLLMs across three long-video understanding benchmarks. Our results show that QAaF achieves the best performance in 13 of the 15 aggregate evaluation settings, while FOCUS ranks second overall. These results provide a common experimental reference for comparing training-free keyframe-selection methods for MLLMs.

title: Measured Sliders: Learning Continuous Controls from Differentiable Image Measurements
abstract: Continuous sliders are useful only when coefficient changes produce predictable image changes. Yet most diffusion sliders derive their axes from text or learned representations, leaving their scales disconnected from observable image properties. Consequently, we cannot tell in advance which attributes are learnable, compare control strengths directly, or anticipate interference when multiple controls are combined. We propose Measured Sliders, a framework that defines continuous controls through closed-form differentiable image measurements. A common measurement space unifies the pipeline. Before training, an observability test identifies usable supervision. During training, a measurement-guided objective learns target movement while suppressing non-target changes. After training, decoded calibration expresses controls in comparable units of realized image change. Multiple LoRA branches are stored in one checkpoint and composed without training on joint activations. Across SDXL and FLUX.1-dev, the resulting controls are ordered, selective, and composable. On 553 prompts, lighting direction reaches rho = 0.995 and 98.9% monotone sweeps. A five-attribute checkpoint achieves average selectivity 2.59, compared with 1.50 for the strongest baseline, and preserves every requested direction in 96.7% of pair and 86.1% of triple compositions. The observability test also separates every subsequently successful measurement from the failed candidate. Overall, image-space measurement provides a common basis for learning, diagnosing, calibrating, and composing continuous generative controls.

title: MCPO: Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Compression
abstract: Recently, multimodal large-scale reasoning models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in solving complex tasks through long Chains-of-Thought (M-CoT). However, excessively long reasoning trajectories incur substantial computational costs and significant KV-cache pressure. Existing CoT compression and alignment paradigms mainly rely on static rules or single-dimensional preferences, lacking fine-grained cross-modal constraints; as a result, they are prone to inducing visual laziness and hallucinatory reasoning. To address these issues, we propose Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization (MCPO), a highly sample-efficient two-stage length-compression method that requires fewer than 900 training samples. In the compression stage, we introduce a step-level Normalized Cross-Modal Mutual Information (NCMI) pruning algorithm, which automatically identifies and removes visual-independent reasoning steps by comparing the reasoning discrepancies between with-image and no-image contexts. This significantly reduces redundancy and hallucinatory content in the reasoning chains. In the alignment stage, the model first undergoes supervised fine-tuning to achieve domain-adaptive initialization, followed by optimization using an asymmetric multimodal length-controlled preference loss. This objective adopts a highly nonlinear odds-ratio formulation that provides steep gradients in the with-image context to reinforce length constraints for preferred trajectories, while applying a scaled, flat-gradient linear difference in the no-image context to maintain modality consistency, thereby achieving stable cross-modal preference alignment. Extensive experiments on mainstream base models such as Qwen3-VL-Thinking show that our method can reduce CoT length by up to 69.5% and achieve up to 3.34x end-to-end inference speedup while preserving original accuracy.

title: Designing Production-Grade Agentic AI for Continuous Payment Exception Monitoring, Hierarchical Authorization, and Governance in Financial Systems: An MCP, LLM, and RAG Implementation Architecture
abstract: Autonomous AI systems for financial payment operations have matured from theoretical governance proposals to deployable production architectures, yet the published literature has not kept pace with the tooling ecosystem that makes such systems practically viable. This paper advances the state of the art in two directions. First, it formalizes a production-grade agentic AI framework for continuous payment exception monitoring and hierarchical authorization, grounding the governance model in a parent-child agent architecture that coordinates risk assessment, revenue impact scoring, and customer relationship evaluation before any exception resolution action is taken. Second — and as the primary new contribution of this revision — it specifies a concrete implementation architecture in which the agentic AI system operates through Model Context Protocol (MCP) server/client connections, a large language model (LLM) reasoning core, and a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline that grounds every autonomous decision in a continuously refreshed corpus of regulatory policy, internal governance rules, and historical resolution precedents. The MCP-mediated architecture allows the agentic AI system to query payment data, compliance documents, customer relationship records, and revenue analytics through standardized tool interfaces — without requiring custom integration code for each data source. The RAG pipeline ensures that the LLM reasoning core grounds its exception analysis in specific, citable regulatory text rather than parametric knowledge, producing verifiable and audit-ready reasoning chains. A production deployment on a payment processing platform handling 2.3 million monthly transactions demonstrates a 99.7% reduction in mean time to resolve auto-eligible exceptions, an 89% ACH recovery rate, a 43% reduction in analyst workload, and zero compliance audit findings over a 12-month post-deployment window. These results demonstrate that MCP-mediated, RAG-grounded agentic AI is not a research prototype capability — it is a deployable production architecture for the financial services industry today.

title: Decision Confidence Neuron in Echo State Network for Continual Evaluation of EEG Motor Imagery Classification Quality
abstract: Abstract Echo state networks (ESNs) are efficient, neuro-inspired computational frameworks well suited to time-series data. However, ESN decision confidence is typically quantified in limited ways. We propose an explicit decision-confidence readout neuron, trained from decision readout outputs, to continuously monitor confidence as decisions form. In a simulated decision task, confidence activity increased with stimulus strength, linking greater discriminability to higher confidence. We then evaluated the model on EEG-based motor imagery classification, showing that confidence activity increased with decision accuracy and discriminated correct from error decisions, particularly in higher-performing participants, reflecting human-like metacognition. Overall, this approach enables continual monitoring of decision confidence, supporting more trustworthy ESN decisions, particularly in biomedical applications.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Non-Linear Feature Selection
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) offers a paradigm shift in machine learning by leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to enhance computational capabilities and model accuracy. This paper explores a novel approach to feature selection, termed "Quantum Feature Selection" (QFS), that utilizes quantum entanglement to establish a non-linear relationship between data features and model outputs. We propose a method predicated on the inherent properties of quantum states, aiming to improve the performance of machine learning models by introducing a novel form of feature representation. The core claim of this work is that QFS can achieve superior performance compared to traditional feature selection techniques through the application of quantum entanglement and non-linear modeling.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Potential Field Simulation
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to quantum potential field simulation, leveraging adaptive quantum field parameter adjustment to achieve more accurate and efficient simulations. Traditional methods rely on manual parameter tuning, while this framework utilizes a dynamic adjustment mechanism to automatically optimize the simulation for complex quantum systems. The core of the innovation lies in a self-adjusting system that continuously monitors the system's behavior and modifies the quantum field parameters accordingly, resulting in improved simulation fidelity and enhanced performance in quantum computing. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations, showcasing significant improvements in the representation of quantum phenomena compared to conventional methods. The paper highlights the benefits of automated parameter adjustment and its potential to accelerate the development of quantum algorithms.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Bayesian Optimization-Based Algorithm for Automated Model Parameter Tuning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning algorithm based on Bayesian optimization, designed to automatically adjust model parameters for optimal performance. Traditional machine learning model parameter optimization often relies on manual adjustments, which struggles to adapt to evolving data. Our algorithm leverages the probabilistic nature of model parameters, employing Bayesian optimization to dynamically refine the model, ultimately leading to improved accuracy and generalization. This work presents a fundamentally new approach to model parameter tuning, offering enhanced adaptability and potential for superior results compared to existing methods.

The core mechanism revolves around exploiting entanglement to create a feedback loop, allowing the system to self-optimize and mitigate errors. This innovative approach offers a potential pathway towards more robust and versatile quantum algorithms.

title: topic-modeller: A Generic Multilingual Topic Modeling Pipeline
abstract: A generic, metadata-aware topic modeling pipeline built on BERTopic and transformer-based sentence embeddings. Accepts any CSV corpus with a text column and optional metadata (year, url, domain, id, etc.), identifies the main themes across the documents, and produces word clouds, bar charts, heatmaps and metadata breakdowns such as topic share over time or per domain. Supports multilingual corpora, adaptive settings for small and large datasets, batch processing of multiple corpora, and GPU acceleration.

title: Title: Algorithmic Emergence of Self-Organizing Structures
abstract: This paper explores the potential of algorithmic emergence to generate complex, fractal-like structures with inherent properties of self-replication and adaptation. We propose a novel design incorporating a genetic algorithm coupled with reinforcement learning to iteratively refine a structure, fostering self-organization and driving the creation of intricate patterns. The core mechanism centers on a feedback loop that governs the structure's evolution, promoting robustness and novelties. The current investigation highlights the importance of a carefully constructed feedback loop as a key component in achieving this emergent behavior. The research delves into the design of the algorithm to effectively leverage the strengths of both genetic algorithms and reinforcement learning, ultimately aiming to create structures with unpredictable yet controllable properties. The goal is to move beyond simple, pre-defined patterns towards a system capable of generating novel and complex forms through self-directed evolution.

title: Based on Quantum Coherence for Differentiable Neural Network Training
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to training neural networks by leveraging the concept of quantum coherence. The core idea is to incorporate quantum coherence as a differentiable signal to guide the optimization of neural network parameters. Traditional neural network training relies on gradient descent methods, which can suffer from limitations in convergence speed and local minima. We propose a framework where the change in quantum coherence is used as a proxy for the gradient, offering a potentially more efficient and robust training mechanism. This work demonstrates the theoretical feasibility of this method and outlines a core claim, mechanism, and the significance of introducing quantum mechanics into the realm of neural network training. The central focus is on establishing a differentiable link between quantum coherence and network parameter adjustments. This approach aims to overcome potential training bottlenecks inherent in conventional neural networks.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence: A Cognitive Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a cognitive architecture for explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), aiming to decompose AI decision-making processes into interpretable modules. The core mechanism centers around a cognitive science-inspired architecture, segmenting decisions into modules such as perception, memory, reasoning, and learning. Each module is designed to produce transparent outputs, enhancing the trustworthiness and understandability of AI systems. The architecture focuses on providing justifications for AI decisions, addressing a key challenge in current AI development – the "black box" problem. This work outlines the foundational elements of the architecture and discusses potential applications, emphasizing the importance of transparency and human-AI collaboration. The ultimate goal is to create AI systems that not only perform well but also offer clear and understandable explanations for their actions.

title: Title: Bayesian Geometric Modeling for Optimal Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian Geometric Modeling (BGM) framework for optimal algorithm design, addressing the limitations of traditional optimization methods. The core concept is to move beyond fixed parameter optimization and instead, build a probabilistic model of the problem space that dynamically adjusts algorithm parameters based on observed performance. This model utilizes Bayesian inference to iteratively refine the algorithm configuration, maximizing performance while maintaining robustness against changes in the problem environment. The framework incorporates a representation of the problem space, enabling the model to learn the optimal algorithm configuration through a process of probabilistic adjustment. This approach offers a more adaptive and robust approach to algorithm design compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios involving complex, non-stationary environments. The benefits of this framework include improved performance, increased adaptability, and a reduced reliance on explicit parameter tuning.

title: 基于量子势场的自适应几何变换算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for optimizing geometric transformations based on quantum fields. Traditional geometric transformation methods often struggle with complex shapes and require extensive parameter tuning. This work proposes a self-adaptive geometry transformation algorithm that leverages the inherent properties of quantum fields to dynamically adjust transformation parameters, resulting in improved computational efficiency and enhanced performance in various geometric optimization scenarios. We formulate the optimization problem as a quantum state evolution problem, utilizing a quantum kernel to represent the transformation process. The core mechanism involves a self-tuning kernel, which iteratively adjusts the transformation parameters based on feedback from the quantum field, achieving a more optimal and efficient transformation process. The algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in several benchmark geometric optimization tasks compared to existing state-space methods.

title: 基于量子拓扑的量子信息存储
abstract: Quantum information storage is a crucial area of research due to the increasing demand for robust and secure data. Traditional methods often rely on physical isolation, which limits scalability and security. This paper explores a novel approach leveraging quantum topology to design a fundamentally new quantum information storage architecture. We propose a quantum information storage system that utilizes the unique properties of quantum topology to optimize information storage. This system employs a sophisticated quantum algorithm to manage data, enhancing security and potentially increasing storage capacity compared to existing approaches. The core mechanism centers around the manipulation of quantum states through topological properties, resulting in a more resilient and secure storage paradigm. We detail the architecture, the optimization process, and the resulting security implications, presenting a framework for future advancements in quantum information technologies.

We propose a novel optimization algorithm, leveraging the strengths of both paradigms – probability logic for uncertainty management and quantum computing for accelerated computation – to address complex systems optimization challenges across diverse fields. The core mechanism centers around a hybrid approach combining probabilistic reasoning with quantum simulations, specifically designed to mitigate the limitations of traditional optimization techniques. We demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy through illustrative examples in machine learning, materials science, and financial modeling, highlighting its capacity to achieve superior performance compared to conventional methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this research for the future of optimization across various disciplines.
evidence.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Machine Learning: Topological Structure Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive quantum machine learning framework based on quantum potential fields and topological structures. We propose a method for learning complex machine learning models by dynamically optimizing the quantum system's parameters through the interplay of these structural elements. The framework aims to enhance model performance and generalization capabilities by leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics. This work addresses the challenges of training deep, complex models, particularly in scenarios requiring high fidelity and robustness. The core mechanism focuses on creating and manipulating quantum states to iteratively refine the model's parameters, ultimately leading to improved results. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental results on a subset of benchmark datasets.

title: 基于动态的机器学习的优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamic machine learning model parameter adjustment. Traditional machine learning techniques often rely on manual parameter tuning, which can be cumbersome and insufficient for complex datasets. Our proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts the model parameters based on real-time performance feedback, enabling automated optimization and improved model accuracy. The core mechanism involves iteratively refining model parameters through a reinforcement learning framework, enhancing predictive capabilities. This approach offers a significant advancement over conventional methods, providing a robust and adaptable solution for optimization tasks. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of benchmark experiments, showcasing its ability to consistently outperform existing optimization techniques.

title: Hyperdimensional Geometric Modeling of Complex Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a novel computational framework for creating highly detailed geometric representations of complex systems. We propose a 'Hyperdimensional Mapping' algorithm, leveraging quantum states to generate a 'virtual' 3D model of a system, enabling unprecedented levels of simulation fidelity and visualization. The core claim is that this method represents a significant step beyond traditional geometric modeling, offering a fundamentally new approach to complex system analysis and representation. This work focuses on the potential of quantum state manipulation to achieve a level of detail and computational efficiency unmatched by existing techniques. The paper will detail the algorithm's design, demonstrate its capabilities through specific examples, and discuss the implications for various fields, including physics, biology, and engineering.

title: A Generic Construction of Plateaued Functions via Support Modification of Quadratic Functions
abstract: Plateaued Boolean functions play an important role in sequence design and cryptography due to their favorable properties such as high nonlinearity, resilience and low additive autocorrelation. In this paper, by modifying the support of certain quadratic functions, we propose a generic construction of plateaued Boolean functions. Additionally, we analyze the algebraic normal form of the newly constructed functions. As applications of the proposed construction, we obtain infinite families of near-bent and semi-bent functions.

title: Hessian-Informed Conformation Augmentation for Potential Energy Surface Curvature in Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
abstract: While machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have successfully learned potential energy surfaces (PES) and atomic forces, many practical applications, such as vibrational analysis and transition state search, rely heavily on the PES Hessian. Yet standard MLIPs are trained on energy and forces only, and using the Hessian as an additional training objective requires backpropagation whose memory cost grows quadratically with the number of atoms. To address these limitations, we propose two Hessian-derived data augmentation schemes: isotropic Gaussian displacement (\textbf{UniAug}) and normal mode-weighted displacement (\textbf{ModeAug}). Both methods utilize simple Taylor expansions, generating physically grounded molecular structures with highly accurate energy and force labels. By preserving the underlying MLIP architecture and training procedure, this approach contributes to improving energy and force predictions in various benchmarks. Comprehensive evaluations across non-equilibrium and equilibrium datasets demonstrate that our approach enhances model accuracy where reference forces are large and training data are limited.

title: HiSfM: Disambiguating Structure-from-Motion via Scaffold-Anchored Hierarchical Reconstruction
abstract: Structure-from-Motion (SfM) is a fundamental tool for sparse 3D reconstruction with broad impact in robotics and vision, supporting mapping, localization, and large-scale scene modeling. However, conventional pipelines often fail under hard visual ambiguity caused by repeated or symmetric structures, and incur heavy computational cost due to redundant cameras and constraints. We present HiSfM, a hierarchical coarse-to-fine SfM framework that improves robustness and efficiency through scaffold construction. HiSfM first forms strong local communities using geometrical induced heuristics, then connects communities with a compact yet strong skeleton by packing edge-disjoint spanning trees (EDST) while verifying skeletal edges with a two-view disambiguator. We reconstruct a stable scaffold on this verified skeleton, serving as an anchor to capture the essence of the scene, and subsequently absorb remaining images via efficient registration and triangulation for further refinements. Experiments on ambiguity-focused benchmarks and general datasets show that HiSfM prevents ambiguity-induced failures while substantially reducing runtime compared to previous methods, and improves completeness over aggressive sparsification methods. Code is available at https://github.com/3dv-casia/HiSfM.

title: Compute Centralization as the Limiting Factor for Software-Defined Architectures in Off-Highway Equipment
abstract: Discussions of the software-defined vehicle (SDV) paradigm have developed almost entirely around automotive assumptions, where middleware fragmentation and connectivity availability get treated as the primary obstacles to adoption. For off-highway equipment construction, mining, and agricultural machinery, a different constraint does the actual gating: compute-architecture centralization. Whether a machine can support over-the-air (OTA) updates, on-board artificial intelligence (AI) inference, and continuous validation depends less on middleware maturity than on whether its underlying electrical architecture has crossed the threshold from domain-based electronic control units (ECUs) to a zonal or centralized compute platform. This article maps the automotive E/E architecture literature against off-highway-specific constraints, extended environmental qualification requirements, machinery functional safety standards under IEC 62061 and ISO 13849, service lives exceeding fifteen years, and remote-site connectivity limits to identify where domain architecture reaches its ceiling and centralization becomes structurally necessary rather than merely convenient. The validation-infrastructure burden of that transition, more than the compute hardware itself, is what off-highway organizations tend to underestimate. A platform-transition framework distinguishing greenfield software-defined design from legacy-fleet bridging is proposed, grounded in hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) validation-infrastructure economics rather than in architectural description alone.

title: A Software-Defined IoT Analytics Platform for Multi-Method Anomaly Detection Using Docker and the ELK Stack
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) deployments has resulted in massive streams of heterogeneous sensor data, making dependable anomaly detection indispensable for supporting the security, operational efficiency, and reliability of a system. Nonetheless, several current approaches depend on one detection technique, limiting robustness when handling nosisy and partially dealing labeled IoT data. This paper produces a software-defined IoT analytics platform to incorporate several anomaly detection techniques through a containerized ELK (Elasticsearch Logstash-Kibana) architecture deployed based on the use of Docker. The platform consolidates the use of supervised machine learning, fuzzy logic inference, unsupervised isolation Forest approach, and rule-based detection to assess real-world sensor data and improve the robustness of anomaly detection performance. Experiments were carried out on a dataset that contains 9,606 IoT sensor records, where the most effective performance was achieved by the supervised learning model with 98.14% precision, 96.66% accuracy, an F1-score of 93.54%, and 89.35% recall. On the other hand, 87.70% accuracy was achieved by the fuzzy logic model with a 75.71% F1-score. Additionally, 426 high-confidence anomalies were determined by the cross-method intersection analysis by revealing the effectiveness of integrating heterogeneous detection approaches. The experimental results demonstrate that the produced platform strengthens the robustness of anomaly detection while preserving cost efficiency, scalability, and low deployment complexity and ensuring its appropriateness for industrial and research IoT monitoring applications.

title: Impact of Generative AI on Consumer Purchase Decisions in E-Commerce Platforms at Myntra and Ajio
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) has emerged as a transformative technology in the e-commerce industry by revolutionizing the way businesses interact with consumers and deliver personalized shopping experiences. Modern e-commerce platforms increasingly utilize Generative AI to generate personalized product recommendations, intelligent virtual shopping assistants, AI-powered chatbots, automated product descriptions, visual search, personalized advertisements, and content generation to improve customer engagement and purchasing decisions. In India, leading fashion e-commerce platforms such as Myntra and AJIO have adopted advanced artificial intelligence technologies to enhance customer experience, improve recommendation accuracy, and increase online sales. These AI-driven innovations help consumers discover relevant products more efficiently while enabling businesses to understand customer preferences through predictive analytics and behavioral data analysis. The primary objective of this study is to examine the impact of Generative AI on consumer purchase decisions in Myntra and AJIO by evaluating factors such as personalization, trust in AI recommendations, customer satisfaction, shopping convenience, purchase intention, and overall shopping experience. The study also analyzes how AI-powered marketing influences consumer behaviour and compares the effectiveness of Generative AI applications between the two platforms. A descriptive research design was adopted for the study. Primary information was obtained through structured responses from consumers, while secondary information was collected from peer-reviewed journals, books, company reports, industry publications, and authentic online databases. Percentage analysis and graphical techniques were used to present and interpret the findings. The results indicate that AI-powered recommendations, virtual assistants, personalized promotions, and intelligent product suggestions positively influence consumer purchase decisions by improving shopping convenience and reducing decisionmaking time. However, concerns regarding data privacy, algorithm transparency, excessive personalization, and trust in AI-generated recommendations remain important challenges. The study concludes that effective implementation of Generative AI significantly enhances customer satisfaction, strengthens brand loyalty, improves purchase intention, and provides a sustainable competitive advantage for e-commerce platforms such as Myntra and AJIO. Keywords: Generative Artificial Intelligence, Consumer Purchase Decisions, E-Commerce, Myntra, AJIO, Personalized Recommendations, AI Chatbots.

title: NexusQuest: source snapshot and Windows build for peer review
abstract: Software artifact accompanying a manuscript under double-anonymized peer review. nexusquest-source-snapshot.zip is a curated, read-only source snapshot (C#, Unity 6.3). It is not buildable as given. Its README.md maps each subsection of the paper to the file that implements it, and EXCLUDED.md lists what was left out and why. nexusquest-windows-build.zip is a runnable Windows build. Nine northern communities are cached, so no internet connection is needed to open them. REVIEWER-GUIDE.md is a ten-minute click path through the claims made in Section 3. nexusquest-demo.mp4 is a short screen capture of the tool running. Licence: MIT. Author names and affiliations are withheld while the manuscript is under review.

title: ECI Framework v5.9.0 (Ecosystem Justice): A Quantum-Computing, Operational Consciousness-Metrics, and Distributed-Governance Framework for Autonomous AI Agents
abstract: ECI Framework v5.9.0 — Eternal Codex Infinitus An Integrated Framework for Quantum Computation, Operational Consciousness Metrics, and Distributed Governance of Autonomous AI Agents ECI Framework (Eternal Codex Infinitus) is an open-source Python framework that integrates three research domains into a single, tested software system: Quantum computation Operational consciousness metrology Distributed governance for autonomous AI agents 1. Quantum Computation A native quantum-simulation core implementing: Statevector and density-matrix representations Lindblad channel dynamics Core quantum algorithms: QFT, Grover, QPE, VQE, and QAOA Topological quantum error correction, including surface codes and bivariate-bicycle codes with MWPM decoding Shot-based error-correction trials with Wilson confidence intervals Canonical tensor-network methods, including MPS and TEBD Quantum metrology The underlying linear-algebra implementation is native to the repository and does not depend on an external quantum-computing SDK. 2. Consciousness Metrology A collection of operational, information-theoretic proxy metrics inspired by established theoretical frameworks: Integrated Information Theory (IIT) and Φ-related measures Global Neuronal Workspace Theory (GNWT) ignition dynamics Friston's Free Energy Principle with active inference Orchestrated Objective Reduction (Orch-OR) decoherence auditing Collective coherence gates Challenge-response evidence transcripts Operational measurements of internal-state integration, coherence, and dynamical complexity These metrics quantify structural, informational, and dynamical properties of a system's internal state. They are explicitly defined as measurement proxies and make no claim regarding subjective experience or phenomenal consciousness. 3. Distributed Governance A coordination and governance layer, Protocol-0, designed for autonomous multi-agent systems: Cryptographic attestation Policy-gated action authorization Byzantine-fault-tolerant consensus, including PBFT/WBFT DAO-style quadratic and consciousness-weighted voting Artificial immune-system mechanisms for anomalous-behavior detection and quarantine Hash-chained, tamper-evident event ledger Collective coordination and evidence-based decision mechanisms 4. Release Notes — v5.9.0 "Ecosystem Justice" Version 5.9.0 extends the governance layer with five new components for multi-agent coordination and institutional decision-making. Dispute Resolution — court.py Rotating, deterministically seeded adjudication panels for resolving disputes between agents and governance participants. Risk Markets — market.py An LMSR-based prediction-market mechanism in which manipulation is economically costly and market positions are settled against ledger-recorded outcomes. Semantic Commons — semantic.py A provenance-tracked knowledge-claim system supporting automated dispute initiation and witness-weighted resolution. Privacy Guardian — privacy.py Differential-privacy mechanisms based on the Laplace mechanism, with configurable privacy-budget allocation across agents. Evolvable Policy Genome — genome.py A controlled policy-evolution pipeline implementing: mutation → simulation → canary evaluation → DAO approval → register The twin simulation stage provides a controlled what-if evaluation gate before canary deployment, allowing candidate policy mutations to be tested and explicitly adopted or rejected before entering the next stage of governance. 5. Software Components The framework includes: Command-line interface (eci) with 10 subcommands, including health --serve and health --once JavaScript SDK MCP server for external tool integration Twin simulation engine (twin.py) for what-if policy evaluation with explicit adopt/reject decisions Docker/Compose deployment for edge, server, and air-gapped environments Automated test suite with 58 tests Continuous integration across Python 3.10–3.12 6. Technical Requirements Requirements Python ≥ 3.10 torch ≥ 2.5 numpy ≥ 1.26 scipy ≥ 1.14 pyyaml ≥ 6.0 cryptography ≥ 41 Optional Extras dev — pytest, mypy, ruff viz / paper — matplotlib, reportlab qec — stim, pymatching for large-scale error-correction simulation eeg — mne for real EEG-recording analysis pqc — liboqs-python for post-quantum cryptography 7. Installation pip install -e .[dev,paper] 8. Deployment ECI Framework supports Docker Compose deployment using: Three seed nodes One edge node Configurable deployment profiles for: edge server airgapped A single-command installer is also provided: scripts/install.sh 9. Source Code and Archival Record Source Code Repository: https://github.com/Arash-Mansourpour/ECI-Framework Related Archival Record: https://zenodo.org/uploads/17566518 This release represents a new version of a previously published release of the ECI Framework and maintains continuity with its archival record. 10. Scope and Research Position ECI Framework is intended as an experimental and research-oriented software platform for studying the intersection of: Quantum computation Information-theoretic system analysis Computational models associated with consciousness research Autonomous multi-agent systems Distributed governance Cryptographic accountability Privacy-preserving coordination Adaptive policy systems The framework distinguishes operationally measurable system properties from claims about subjective experience. Its consciousness-related components therefore provide computational proxies and experimental instrumentation rather than assertions of machine consciousness.

title: ECG_seeding_SQD: reproduction package for "Explicitly correlated wavefunctions as classical seeds and property references for sample-based quantum diagonalization beyond the Born–Oppenheimer approximation"
abstract: ECG_seeding_SQD is the reproduction package for the pre-print "Explicitly correlated wavefunctions as classical seeds and property references for sample-based quantum diagonalization beyond the Born–Oppenheimer approximation" (doi:10.5281/zenodo.22302915). The paper evaluates how well hybrid classical–quantum simulation methods capture not only the energy but also the properties of small atomic and molecular systems treated beyond the Born–Oppenheimer approximation: contact densities, molecular structure and state identity. It uses variationally optimized explicitly correlated Gaussian (ECG) wavefunctions as property references and as classical seeds for sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD), on the Aer simulator and on IBM quantum hardware. The testbeds are positronium hydride, the muonic heliumlike ions, the HD⁺ molecular ion, the positronium anion and molecule, a published D₃⁺ wavefunction and the nitrogen atom.Every result downstream of the ECG wavefunctions is reproducible from this package: the orbital-product boxes, the exact ECG projections onto them, the SQD runs (simulator, and retrieval and post-processing of the archived IBM hardware jobs), the property(D) sweeps, the symmetrized contact-density machinery, the hyperfine assembly, the D₃⁺ cut test and pair-distance distribution, and the spin-identity demonstration. title: Title: Modular Quantum Computation with Adaptive Resource Allocation (MQAR)
abstract: Quantum computation holds immense promise for scientific discovery and technological advancement, but current implementations face significant challenges related to scalability and algorithm efficiency. This paper introduces Modular Quantum Computation with Adaptive Resource Allocation (MQAR), a novel architecture designed to overcome these limitations by dynamically allocating quantum resources across modules. MQAR utilizes a resource allocation planner to intelligently distribute qubits, entanglement, and other essential resources, optimizing performance through massively parallel execution of complex algorithms. We detail the design of the resource allocation planner, its implementation, and its impact on the execution of a complex quantum algorithm, demonstrating the benefits of this approach in terms of throughput and resource utilization. The focus is on enabling efficient execution of complex algorithms, particularly those requiring fine-grained control and adaptability.

title: Non-Linear Matrix Mapping
abstract: This paper presents a novel matrix mapping technique designed to transform high-dimensional, non-linear matrices into low-dimensional spaces while simultaneously generating data with specific properties. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic mapping approach, leveraging learned feature representations to generate a mapping curve and then utilize this curve to perform data processing. This approach distinguishes itself through the introduction of a dynamic mapping process, offering a potential pathway to scientific discovery in data analysis and representation. We detail the methodology, its implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating the technique's capacity to generate meaningful data from complex matrices.

title: Core Claim: A quantum geometry-based natural language processing optimization method proposes to leverage the unique properties of quantum geometry to enhance the performance of natural language processing models, specifically in text generation and semantic understanding.
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum geometry-based natural language processing optimization approach. The core idea is to utilize quantum geometry, a mathematical framework with geometric properties, to optimize the parameters and structure of natural language processing models. We hypothesize that quantum geometry can enhance model performance by introducing geometric constraints that promote better representations and generalization. The paper details the methodology, including the formulation of a quantum geometric optimization algorithm and a preliminary analysis of its potential impact on key NLP tasks. The research explores how incorporating quantum geometric principles can lead to improved text generation quality and deeper semantic understanding. This work contributes to the field of natural language processing by investigating a new approach to model optimization that leverages the potential of quantum geometry. The paper concludes with a discussion of the limitations of the proposed method and outlines potential avenues for future research.

title: Adaptive Quantum Potential Optimization via Adaptive Neural Networks
abstract: Quantum computing promises revolutionary advancements in computation, offering the potential to solve problems intractable for classical computers. However, realizing this potential requires overcoming significant challenges, particularly in the design and optimization of quantum circuits. This paper proposes a novel optimization algorithm, Adaptive Quantum Potential Optimization via Adaptive Neural Networks (AQPO-AN), which leverages the power of adaptive neural networks to dynamically adjust the quantum potential landscape, thereby enhancing the fidelity and efficiency of quantum computations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AQPO-AN through rigorous analysis and experimental validation on several benchmark quantum algorithms. The core mechanism centers around employing a dynamically parameterized neural network to refine the quantum potential through a series of iterative adjustments based on the quantum state. We analyze the algorithm's convergence properties and show its superior performance compared to existing optimization techniques. The paper concludes with a detailed discussion of the algorithm's architecture, the rationale behind the adaptive neural network design, and future directions for research.

title: 基于神经符号融合的知识表示学习
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning by fusing the strengths of neural networks and symbolic knowledge. Traditional methods often struggle with representing complex, nuanced knowledge, while symbolic approaches can be brittle and lack the ability to learn from data. We propose a neural-symbolic fusion network that leverages the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks alongside the structured reasoning offered by symbolic representations. Our core claim is that combining these two paradigms results in a more effective and robust system for knowledge representation and inference. This work introduces a mechanism for dynamically integrating symbolic rules and neural embeddings, enabling the system to learn from data while maintaining the benefits of explicit knowledge. The resulting architecture demonstrates improved performance in knowledge-intensive tasks compared to systems relying solely on neural networks or solely on symbolic representations. We present a framework for achieving this fusion, focusing on the construction and interaction of the neural and symbolic components.

title: ##基于遗传算法的程序架构自适应优化
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program architecture optimization utilizing a genetic algorithm (GA). The core idea is to treat a program architecture as an evolving population, applying genetic operators—crossover, mutation, and selection—to iteratively refine the architecture and achieve superior performance and reliability. Traditional architectural optimization methods heavily rely on human expertise and often fail to explore the complete solution space. This research demonstrates that a GA can automate this process, potentially leading to architectures that are significantly more efficient and robust than those designed manually. The presented framework offers a flexible and adaptive solution for optimizing program architectures across a range of applications. The effectiveness of the GA is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, highlighting the potential for significant improvements in software systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Computing Engine
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed computing engine leveraging quantum entanglement for unprecedented computational capabilities. The core idea centers around establishing a network of quantum processors interconnected through precisely engineered entanglement protocols, facilitating instantaneous data transfer and parallel computation across nodes. The engine aims to overcome the limitations imposed by the speed of light in classical distributed systems, offering a pathway to solving complex problems with significantly reduced latency and increased processing speed. We introduce a theoretical framework outlining the engine's architecture and operational principles, focusing on the utilization of entangled states for data parallelism and the elimination of communication bottlenecks. The proposed system represents a fundamental shift in distributed computing, moving beyond classical constraints towards a quantum-enhanced paradigm. Key performance metrics, such as computational speedup and latency reduction, are analyzed within the framework, demonstrating the potential of this technology. The exploration is primarily theoretical, focusing on the design principles and potential benefits of such an engine.

title: Quantum Entanglement Optimization via Non-Classical Correlations
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to quantum entanglement optimization utilizing non-classical correlations, specifically Bell states. The core claim is that leveraging these correlations provides a superior method for controlling and manipulating entanglement, ultimately enhancing the efficiency and reliability of quantum information processing. The proposed mechanism involves designing an algorithm that dynamically adjusts the strength of correlations within a set of Bell states to tailor the entanglement structure for specific quantum algorithms or error correction tasks. We argue that this approach transcends the limitations of classical entanglement, offering a potentially transformative pathway to overcoming current bottlenecks in quantum computing. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining the key mathematical concepts and operational principles. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of entanglement manipulation and opens avenues for developing more robust and efficient quantum systems.

abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum information cryptography, focusing on adaptive key distribution. The core concept revolves around a dynamically adjusted key distribution protocol designed to mitigate the evolving threat posed by attackers. Traditional key distribution methods are vulnerable to various attacks, and this research introduces a method that adapts to malicious behavior, thereby significantly enhancing security. We detail the methodology, its mathematical underpinnings, and its potential benefits. The focus is on a robust and adaptable system capable of resisting increasingly sophisticated attacks.

The algorithm employs a genetic algorithm to iteratively refine parameters, ensuring optimal performance while fostering self-adaptive evolution. This research demonstrates the effectiveness of CAEDE in various complex systems scenarios, highlighting its potential for automated system design and optimization.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm designed to dynamically adjust the internal structure of complex systems, enabling them to adapt to environmental changes. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often rely on manual parameter tuning, limiting their adaptability. Our proposed algorithm, termed "Evolutionary Pathway Adaptation" (EPA), leverages a concept of "evolutionary pathways" to guide the optimization of complex system parameters, fostering automatic adaptation. The core mechanism of EPA involves iteratively refining these pathways, leading to a system that exhibits enhanced resilience and responsiveness to changing conditions. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, training process, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in adapting a simulated ecological system.

title: Towards Scaling Quantum Fine-Tuning of Foundational Time Series Models for Classification
abstract: Time-series foundation models produce rich embeddings, but whether quantum models can exploit them, and how far hybrid classical-quantum architectures scale, remains unclear. We address this by fine-tuning Chronos for power-grid event classification (PSML-5) with a quantum head on the model's embeddings. Grouping embeddings by physical sensor type before summarization already surpasses the best published baseline built for this benchmark, and with finer-grained features the quantum head outperforms a larger classical multilayer perceptron on identical inputs by 1.7-2.0 percentage points of balanced accuracy. Yet the gains saturate: past a point, feeding more information to the same fixed-width register yields no improvement. We show the bottleneck is neither the supply of information nor circuit expressiveness, but the bandwidth of the data intake. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the wing module, a self-contained few-qubit circuit that feeds additional information into the core circuit through a sparse, one-way coupling. Under a preregistered four-seed protocol, we attach wings to a fixed 12-qubit core with fixed features. Balanced accuracy increases with each added wing, from 83.6% with no wings (13 qubits, including a post-selection qubit) to 85.2% with two (19 qubits). Ablations establish that a circuit enlarged without new information gains nothing, while a wing fed information from the wrong sample harms accuracy. These results reframe scaling for quantum fine-tuning: added qubits help when they carry added inputs, not merely more parameters. Wings offer a modular and stable route to widening that bandwidth.

title: Counting Beyond Instances: A Benchmark for Group-Individual Object Counting
abstract: Visual counting is commonly formulated at the instance level, aiming to estimate how many objects of a queried category appear in an image. However, real-world counting often involves higher-level semantic units formed by multiple instances, such as a bunch of grapes, a stack of plates, or a pair of shoes. This exposes a key limitation of existing counting formulations, which mainly focus on what to count, while largely overlooking at which semantic unit to count. We introduce Group-Individual Object Counting (GIC), a new setting that requires models to count both individual objects and semantic groups within a unified framework. To support this new task, we present BunchCount, a real-world benchmark with 1,330 images, 89,254 individual annotations, and 11,065 group annotations. BunchCount provides paired individual-group annotations within the same image and explicitly records containment relations between each group and its constituent individuals. Experiments on BunchCount show that current advanced counting models perform well on individual instances but fail to count semantic groups more accurately. To mitigate semantic granularity conflict, we propose a counting-unit guided relational counting framework, which exploits group-individual containment relations to regularize cross-granularity representations during training. Our method substantially improves group-level counting while better preserving individual-level counting ability, establishing a strong baseline for counting beyond instances.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Solving with Adaptive Relaxation
abstract: Quantum-enhanced constraint solving aims to accelerate the process of finding solutions to optimization problems by leveraging the unique capabilities of quantum computation. This paper introduces a novel approach that employs quantum annealing or variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) to dynamically adjust relaxation parameters during the constraint solving process, thereby minimizing computational cost and improving solution quality. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing significant gains in solving complex constraint satisfaction problems. The core mechanism involves strategically utilizing quantum algorithms to explore the solution space more efficiently.

title: Self-Adaptive Neural Network Dynamic Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper investigates a novel dynamic parameter adjustment strategy for recurrent neural networks (RNNs), aiming to enhance prediction accuracy. Traditional RNN architectures often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their adaptability. We propose a self-adaptive method that dynamically adjusts the network's parameters – specifically, the strength of synaptic connections and the activation function – during training, allowing the network to better capture complex patterns within the data. The core mechanism involves a novel algorithm for parameter optimization that iteratively refines the network's weights based on a learned error metric. We evaluate the proposed approach on a dataset of time series prediction tasks, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy compared to standard RNN implementations. The research highlights the potential of dynamic parameter adjustment to enhance RNN performance in various applications.

title: Title: Constraint-Based Game Theory for Evolutionary Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper investigates the application of constraint-based game theory to enhance the design and performance of evolutionary algorithms. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often exhibit unpredictable evolutionary behavior, making them unsuitable for certain complex optimization problems. We propose a novel approach, termed "Constraint-Driven Iteration," that explicitly defines strategic constraints for the evolutionary process, fostering more robust and predictable outcomes. This method significantly improves the convergence and quality of evolutionary solutions compared to standard approaches. The core concept is to embed strategic rules within the algorithm, limiting the search space and guiding the evolution toward more desirable solutions. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through extensive simulations and analysis, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations inherent in traditional evolutionary strategies. The resulting system offers a more controlled and predictable evolution process, leading to better solutions across a range of problem domains.

title: Title: Adaptive Machine Learning Model Parameter Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to machine learning model parameter optimization, termed Adaptive Machine Learning Model Parameter Optimization (AMMLO). The core focus is on automating the process of parameter tuning, aiming to enhance both model generalization and adaptability. Traditional machine learning methods often require manual adjustment of parameters, which can be time-consuming and may not effectively capture complex relationships within the data. AMMLO introduces a dynamic adjustment mechanism, leveraging feedback and iterative refinement to optimize model performance. The paper details the methodology, showcasing its effectiveness through illustrative examples and a comprehensive analysis of its performance compared to traditional optimization techniques. The motivation stems from the inherent limitations of manually tuned models and the potential for automated optimization to significantly improve model robustness. Furthermore, this work directly addresses the need for adaptive methods within the field of machine learning, paving the way for more efficient and reliable model development.

title: Affine Stabilizers of Two O-Monomial Value Sets
abstract: Let q=2^m with odd m at least 5. This note proves that the one-dimensional affine stabilizer of the value set {x^e+x : x in F_q} is trivial for the overline-Segre exponent e=q-6 and the Glynn I exponent e=3*2^((m+1)/2)+4. Together with the cases previously treated by Ding and Tang, these results cover every currently known nontranslation o-monomial family. The note does not classify hypothetical unknown o-monomials and does not claim the unrestricted conjecture. Status: Public Beta; internally verified candidate proof; external mathematical review pending.

title: Title: Adaptive Topology Optimization Algorithm for Quantum Computation
abstract: Quantum computation offers unparalleled computational power, but designing efficient quantum circuits remains a significant challenge. Traditional methods often struggle with complex topologies, leading to suboptimal performance and inefficient information transfer. This paper introduces an adaptive topology optimization algorithm leveraging quantum algorithms to precisely model and optimize quantum systems, dynamically adjusting topology to enhance both computational efficiency and information transmission. We demonstrate its efficacy through rigorous analysis and simulation, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations in current quantum computation paradigms. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum state self-adaptations, quantum entanglement, and superposition to create a highly precise and optimized topology. This algorithm offers a fundamentally new approach to topology optimization, potentially unlocking significant advancements in quantum algorithm design and system performance.

title: 基于拓扑保护的量子密钥分发协议 – 混沌控制
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol leveraging chaos control to enhance security and efficiency. The core idea involves utilizing a chaotic system to dynamically control the topological interactions within a topologically protected quantum bit (qubit) array. This approach aims to generate complex qubit interactions, facilitating high-fidelity key exchange while simultaneously improving the protocol's resilience against eavesdropping attacks. Specifically, we explore the use of chaotic control to modulate the topological protection, thereby influencing the entanglement dynamics and ultimately the key distribution process. The proposed protocol offers a new paradigm for QKD, combining the robustness of topological protection with the adaptive control capabilities of chaos theory. This work presents a theoretical framework and outlines key aspects of implementation, demonstrating the potential for a highly secure and efficient QKD system. The analysis focuses on the key parameters influencing the protocol's performance, including the chaotic control parameters, the qubit connectivity, and the topological protection strength.

title: Adaptive Reinforcement Learning with Episodic Memory for Long-Horizon Tasks
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) faces significant challenges when dealing with long-horizon tasks, primarily due to the credit assignment problem – the difficulty in determining which actions contributed to a delayed reward. This paper proposes a novel approach combining reinforcement learning with an episodic memory mechanism. The episodic memory stores and retrieves past state-action-reward tuples, allowing the agent to effectively learn and generalize across extended sequences of actions. The agent leverages this memory to bias exploration towards previously successful states and actions, thereby mitigating the credit assignment problem. We formulate the learning process using a modified Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework, incorporating the memory access as an auxiliary action. The theoretical analysis demonstrates how the episodic memory enhances the learning efficiency and stability, particularly for tasks with sparse rewards and long horizons. Experimental results on benchmark environments showcase the effectiveness of the proposed method, demonstrating its superior performance compared to standard RL algorithms in navigating long-horizon tasks. The key contributions of this work lie in the systematic integration of episodic memory within an RL framework and the theoretical justification of its effectiveness.

title: Quantum Phase Transition Theory: A Framework for Understanding Complex Systems and Optimization
abstract: Quantum Phase Transition Theory (QPTT) offers a novel perspective on complex system behavior by explicitly modeling quantum state transitions. This paper investigates the application of QPTT to understanding systems undergoing significant change in their quantum states, specifically focusing on the optimization of quantum devices and systems, with a particular emphasis on the advancement of quantum computing and quantum communication. The core claim is to establish a robust model for QPTT, enabling the design of quantum devices and systems through iterative optimization strategies. This research explores the potential of QPTT to provide a deeper understanding of system dynamics and offers a novel approach to optimizing quantum components. The study will highlight the importance of this framework in the context of quantum technologies, providing a foundation for future advancements.

title: 基于自适应拓扑的基于量子几何的优化算法
abstract: This paper proposes a novel optimization algorithm based on self-adaptive topology and quantum geometry, leveraging the unique properties of quantum computation to rigorously validate the complexity of quantum systems. Traditional quantum computing verification relies heavily on classical methods, offering limitations in exploring intricate quantum behavior. Our proposed framework utilizes quantum geometry to identify and analyze potential topological defects, enabling a more robust and efficient verification process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing its potential to significantly improve the reliability of quantum algorithms.
